label: At D2 after a2 reaches S2, late in the episode, stronger after an unrewarded trial.
short_terms: (in_state + in_action == 4) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.maximum(ep_dec - 5, 0) ;; (in_state + in_action == 4) * belief_lo * np.maximum(ep_dec - 5, 0) ;; (in_state + in_action == 4) * np.maximum(ep_dec - 5, 0)
terms: (in_state + in_action == 4) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.maximum(ep_dec - 5, 0) ;; (in_state + in_action == 4) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (in_state + in_action == 4) * np.maximum(ep_dec - 5, 0) ;; (in_state + in_action == 4) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_action == 2) * np.maximum(ep_dec - 5, 0) ;; (in_state + in_action == 4) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * np.maximum(ep_dec - 5, 0) ;; (in_state + in_action == 4) * (prev_reward == 0) * (ep_trial >= 85) ;; (in_state + in_action == 4) * (prev_reward == 0) * belief_lo * np.maximum(ep_dec - 5, 0) ;; (in_state + in_action == 4) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_state == 1) * np.maximum(ep_dec - 5, 0)
explanation: Sparse feature (nonzero on 1.7% of steps). It is active only at D2 when the agent chose a2 and reached S2 (common), i.e. in_state = in_action = 2. Its size grows steeply with position in the episode: near zero before trial ~50, then rising sharply through trials 60-99. It is much larger when the previous trial was unrewarded: values near 2 late in the episode after r=0, around 0.3 after r=1. A weaker graded part: it is somewhat larger when the ideal observer believes S2 is good (negative weight on belief_lo). D1 and GO are always zero. The free fit adds a step at trial >= 85, a boost when the previous unrewarded trial was also a2, and a reduction when the previous trial was a2 -> S1 (rare). All terms are observed-only (the D2 inputs plus history).

issues: The label leaves out the belief term that is in the short form. Removing (in_state+in_action==4)*belief_lo*ramp drops test R^2 beyond timing from 0.524 to 0.471, so the term is real (negative weight: the feature is larger when the ideal observer favours S2 as the good state). It should be in the label.

The explanation says the feature 'reaches about 2 after r=0'. Only the peaks reach about 2. In misses, every window near 2.0 is D2 a2->S2 where the previous trial was a2->S1 unrewarded (rare, unrewarded): t84, t86, t87, t90. After a common a2->S2 unrewarded trial the feature is only about 0.5-0.75, and the short form predicts about 0.44 at the peaks. The peaks are therefore under-fit by a factor of about 4. Adding last_is('a2 S1 u') as a term, e.g. '(in_state+in_action==4)*last_is('a2 S1 u')*(ep_trial>=80) ;; (in_state+in_action==4)*(prev_reward==0)*np.maximum(ep_dec-5,0) ;; (in_state+in_action==4)*np.maximum(ep_dec-5,0)', gains very little (test 0.532 vs 0.524), because belief_lo already absorbs most of this effect.

Systematic over-prediction at D2 after an unrewarded a1 trial: mean error -0.034 after a1 S1 u, against at most +0.008 in every other cell. So the boost after an unrewarded trial is weaker when the previous choice was a1. But restricting the term to a2-unrewarded (prev_action - prev_reward == 2) scores worse (test 0.444-0.488), so the general claim 'after an unrewarded trial' holds.

The ramp shape is not overfit. np.maximum(ep_dec-5,0), np.maximum(ep_trial-50,0) and np.maximum(ep_trial-60,0) all give test 0.52-0.53; a later onset (ep_trial-70) is worse (0.47). The short form is a real description, not curve fitting. Test 0.524 vs dev 0.53 means no overfit.
